topComments.text: Hi HN, I'm Ivar, creator of Unleash. Unleash started in 2014 as an internal tool at my company at the time, because we wanted to ship to production continuously without big-bang releases. It's an Open-Source feature flag platform with SDKs for >25 languages. A few design choices that might be interesting: - Local evaluation: server-side SDKs fetch the flag config and evaluate in-process, so user data never leaves your app and a flag check is a memory lookup, not a network call. - Shared Rust engine (Yggdrasil): the evaluation logic is written once in Rust and embedded in the SDKs, so behaviour is the same across languages. - Unleash Edge: a Rust proxy/cache for frontend and edge clients at scale. stories.author: LaSombra

topComments.text: Had been looking for this. Thank you

topComments.author: alexkampler
topComments.text: One thing I would add to the intro: calling this "bare metal" is almost a cheat compared to the BIOS days. You start with a working console, a memory map, and even a file system service; then ExitBootServices takes every bit of that away. That is the real bare-metal moment, and it is exactly where a series like this earns its keep. Two things that always bite people on this path: - The memory map key returned by GetMemoryMap goes stale the moment anything allocates. Hand the freshly fetched key straight to ExitBootServices; if it comes back EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER, that is why. The firmware is right, even though it feels unfair. - QEMU with OVMF (code and vars as separate pflash files) gives a far faster edit-run loop than rebooting hardware, and it is stricter about struct layout and protocol revisions than most real firmware. When something boots on metal but not in OVMF, it is almost always an alignment or version assumption, not a QEMU bug. The pragmatic digression in Part 4 was a good call. The gap between "it built" and "it boots" is where most of the learning (and quitting) happens.

infoqArticles.description: GitLab 19.5, released on October 15, puts agentic software development and governance at the centre of the platform, making its GitLab MCP server generally available while expanding how external AI agents can interact with GitLab. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta: Restores the Compiler API and Makes Vue and Svelte First-Class
infoqArticles.description: TypeScript 7.1 Beta, announced October 20, 2026, restores the compiler API removed in 7.0, now split into separate entry points. It adds content mappers, letting tools like Vue check non-standard files. One Vue project's type checks fell from 14.19 to 3.10 seconds. An editor issue remains open, and teams may need TypeScript 6 alongside 7. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: The Socio-Technical Staff+ Engineer: Architecture, Culture and Organisational Change
infoqArticles.description: Vanessa Formicola shares how technical leaders can move beyond "wishful architecture" by practicing holistic socio-technical engineering. She discusses why engineering leaders must account for organizational maturity, reward structures, geopolitical climate, and team dynamics, framing the staff-plus role as designing the conditions for technology to thrive rather than just picking tools. By Vaness
infoqArticles.author: Vanessa Formicola

infoqArticles.title: AWS Ships Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities
infoqArticles.description: AWS has made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available in two regions. The service proves exploitability by running real exploits in a sandbox, then opens fixes as pull requests. Published pricing charges per finding processed as well as per line of code, and practitioners are asking what would justify letting it merge fixes on its own. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Article: Identity as an Architectural Concern: Enterprise IAM Beyond Authentication
infoqArticles.description: The way you design your identities will drive your data models, your service scope, and your revocation policies; enterprise identity management is thus an architectural problem, not an afterthought. Based on our experience in service account governance, this article touches upon graph vs. RBAC, integrating a vault you don't own, and bounding revocation latency for an event stream. By Vaishnavi Kh
infoqArticles.author: Vaishnavi Khosla

infoqArticles.title: Vault Fork OpenBao Adds External Keys and Quantum-Ready TLS
infoqArticles.description: OpenBao has released version 2.7, adding read scaling for PostgreSQL-backed deployments, support for external hardware security module (HSM) and key management service (KMS) keys, and post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. The release also introduces control groups for human review of sensitive operations and new headers intended to keep requests consistent across load-balanced OpenBao nodes. By M
infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: GitHub Actions Lockfiles Reach GA to Secure Workflow Dependencies
infoqArticles.description: GitHub has made workflow dependency lockfiles for GitHub Actions generally available on October 28, 2026, two weeks after the feature entered public preview. Workflows can maintain clear tag and branch references. By Claudio Masolo
infoqArticles.author: Claudio Masolo

infoqArticles.title: Edera's Object Capability Bounded Authority Promises to Isolate Credentials From AI Agent Workloads
infoqArticles.description: Edera announced Object Capability Bounded Authority, a security model that separates an AI agent's or MCP server's required authority from the credentials behind it. Hypervisor-enforced capabilities limit agents to specific actions without storing secrets in the workload. Initial releases cover scoped command execution and workload identity; credential-brokered API access will follow. By Olimpiu P
infoqArticles.author: Olimpiu Pop

infoqArticles.title: Google Cloud API Gateway Introduces Streaming Support for Real-Time and AI-Powered Applications
infoqArticles.description: Google has announced the public preview of streaming support for API Gateway, extending its traditional request-response model to support applications requiring real-time communication. According to Google, this is particularly relevant for AI applications that provide streaming model responses, multi-step agent workflows, and interactive sessions. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Leapwork Play Reaches GA with Governance for Playwright Tests
infoqArticles.description: Leapwork Play adds requirement traceability and approval workflows around portable Playwright tests. Full governance and audit capabilities require an enterprise package. By Mark Silvester
infoqArticles.author: Mark Silvester

infoqArticles.title: Building a Culture for a Kubernetes-Based Platform in a Bank
infoqArticles.description: In banking, open source can earn trust by running real workloads, as Marcy Paramonova and Stéphane Cusin explained in their talk Building Cloud Native Culture in a Bank at KubeCon & CloudNativeCon Europe. Deploying Kubernetes was the easy part; the hard part was culture: community of practice, shared knowledge, rituals, ownership. Teams try things, keep what works, and improve bottom-up. By Ben Li
infoqArticles.author: Ben Linders

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Zero Trust Agent Systems that Pass Audits and Still Ship
infoqArticles.description: Advait Patel shares a playbook for securing AI agent systems in production. He discusses moving defense boundaries from the prompt to the tool layer, enforcing scoped workload identities, and mitigating prompt injection via tool outputs. He explains how to structure audit-ready observability and implement kill switches to protect critical data while keeping deployment fast and compliant. By Advait
infoqArticles.author: Advait Patel

infoqArticles.title: Inkitt Builds a One-Shot PR Creator with Resumable Agent Orchestration
infoqArticles.description: Inkitt built a one-shot pull request creator that automates small, low-risk code changes from task intake to draft PR creation. Its event-driven orchestrator persists workflow state, coordinates short-lived coding agent containers, bounds retries, and enforces permission restrictions while retaining human review and approval before changes can be merged. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Panel: Who Builds the Frontend Now? (And What Breaks When They Do)
infoqArticles.description: The panelists explain how AI tools and vibe coding reshape frontend and mobile engineering. They share insights on evolving junior developer roles, managing AI-generated code review fatigue, designing systems for autonomous agents, enforcing architectural guardrails, and navigating economic shifts in open-source software sustainability. By Luca Mezzalira, James Hall, Danielle An, Ivan Zarea
infoqArticles.author: Luca Mezzalira, James Hall, Danielle An, Ivan Zarea
